mappings.note: Sign of lens power follows from the sign of f, not from image nature. Nearest legal code; power of a lens has no outcome in curriculum 71 (defect list).
Both clauses are about which mirror enlarges and where the object must sit - image characteristics of a concave vs convex mirror, LO-1, with no formula used.

Rectilinear propagation and shadows. No competency or outcome in this frame covers it - not reflection, not refraction, not mirrors or lenses - so only the goal-level code is true. Flagged as a content-area gap.
Real focus of a concave mirror and whether its image is always real: focus definition plus image nature, both inside LO-1's 'locates the image formed by a concave mirror'.
Field of view of a convex mirror as the reason for its use - an image characteristic, not a computed magnification, so LO-1 rather than LO-2.
Whether a mirror's focal length changes with the surrounding medium, plus R = 2f. Closest available outcome; mirror parameters in their own right are not named by any outcome (see defect list).
Concave mirror converging sunlight to its focus - the parallel-ray behaviour that LO-1's image location rests on. No diagram is asked for, so not C 8.1-LO-2.
Tests the statement i = r at normal incidence: the 'states the laws of reflection' clause of LO-1, with no image located and nothing drawn.
Same medium-independence point as the previous pair, asked the other way round. Nearest outcome only - no outcome names mirror focal length as a property.
'What is light?' - the nature of light itself. No competency in this frame reaches it; C 2.3 is about mirrors and lenses, C 5.3 about other subjects. Goal level is the only honest cite.
Light as an electromagnetic wave. Same gap as the previous item: no outcome or competency of curriculum 71 covers the nature of light.
Definition of an image as the meeting point of reflected/refracted rays - the concept LO-1's 'locates the image' rests on, and the answer is framed by reflection first.
Real image defined by actual intersection of rays; this is the nature-of-image half of locating an image, not a formula or a diagram task.
Virtual image defined by apparent intersection - paired with the previous item; LO-1 is the only outcome that speaks of image formation qualitatively.
Bare statement of the first law of reflection for regular reflection. Explicitly the 'states the laws of reflection' clause, with no mirror geometry involved.
Applies i = r to the special case of normal incidence on a plane surface - still the law-of-reflection clause of LO-1, not image location.

Recall of the mirror formula, not a substitution. The frame has no 'states the mirror formula' outcome (unlike LO-1 and LO-3, which both carry a 'states' clause), so the application outcome has to carry it.
Recall of m = h2/h1 = -v/u. Same limitation as the mirror-formula item: LO-2 is the only outcome naming the magnification formula, stating or applying.
One use of each mirror, answered from the image each type forms - the applied end of LO-1's image characteristics, not a formula or a ray diagram.
Why a convex mirror for a side-view: virtual, erect, diminished plus wide field. Reason is the image characteristic, which is LO-1.
Screenability of a virtual image - the real/virtual distinction that LO-1's image location carries. No computation and no diagram.
Definition of the principal focus of a spherical mirror, stated through the parallel-ray behaviour that LO-1 uses to locate images.
Centre of curvature of a convex mirror specifically - the geometric reference LO-1 needs to locate a convex-mirror image; no outcome addresses mirror terminology on its own.
Answered by the object-at-C coincidence rule, not by working the mirror formula, so it stays with the qualitative image-location outcome.
The task is to draw the convex-mirror construction for a parallel incident ray. Drawing is the whole of what is graded, so the ray-diagram outcome, not LO-1.
